products.name: Olaplex Nº.8 Bond Intense Moisture Mask
products.shortDescription: A weekly, wash-out bond-building hair mask that leans on ceramides, hyaluronic acid, and plant oils to hydrate dry, color-treated hair.
products.fullReview:
Olaplex Nº.8 Bond Intense Moisture Mask sits apart from the brand's original Nº.3 Hair Perfector: instead of leading with the bis-aminopropyl diglycol dimaleate bond-building molecule, Nº.8 uses that ingredient in a smaller amount and builds the rest of the formula around hydration. Avocado oil, rice bran oil, rosehip seed extract, ceramides, and hyaluronic acid work alongside the bond-building base to target strands that feel dry, brittle, or dulled by color processing.

Because dimethicone appears near the top of the ingredient list, the mask leaves a noticeably smooth, detangled finish, but that same silicone can be a drawback for anyone trying to avoid buildup-prone ingredients or following a routine that limits non-water-soluble silicones. Olaplex ties its bond-building technology to an independent study reporting gains in shine, hydration, and smoothness after a single use, though results from any single brand-cited study should be read as brand-reported rather than guaranteed for every hair type.

Olaplex positions Nº.8 as usable on all hair types, including hair that has never been colored, which makes it a flexible pick for households sharing one mask. For color-treated or lightened hair specifically, the blend of humectants and emollients is meant to replace weekly conditioner rather than serve as a leave-in or pre-shampoo treatment, so it fits best into a routine that already includes a separate bond-focused step for more compromised hair.

Cost per use is a real consideration: the standard bottle is compact, and thicker or longer hair needs multiple pumps per application, which can shorten how many treatments a single bottle provides. Anyone with fine hair may also find the richness of the formula heavier than a lightweight conditioner, so it is worth patch-testing on a small section first.
pros: Layers ceramides, hyaluronic acid, and plant oils onto Olaplex's bond-building base for added hydration
Positioned by the brand for use on all hair types, including hair that has never been chemically treated
Rinses out after about ten minutes, fitting into an existing weekly conditioning routine
cons: Contains dimethicone, a silicone some low-buildup or curl-focused routines try to avoid
Carries the brand's bond-building ingredient at a lower concentration than in Nº.3, so it is not a substitute for a dedicated bond-repair treatment
products.bestFor: Color-treated or heat-styled hair that needs a weekly moisture boost alongside, not instead of, a separate bond-repair treatment.

products.name: Briogeo Don't Despair, Repair! Deep Conditioning Mask
products.shortDescription: A sulfate-, silicone-, and phthalate-free weekly deep conditioning mask built around Briogeo's NOVA Complex for dry, color-treated hair.
products.fullReview:
Briogeo's Don't Despair, Repair! Deep Conditioning Mask is built around the brand's NOVA Complex, combining B-vitamins, rosehip and argan oils, algae extract, and biotin. Briogeo markets it specifically for dry, damaged, chemically-treated, or lifeless hair, and states the mask is safe for color-treated, keratin-treated, and relaxed hair, which makes it a reasonable weekly pick for people managing dye-related dryness.

The formula is free of sulfates, silicones, and phthalates and is described as 98% naturally derived, so it suits readers who are trying to limit buildup-prone ingredients or who follow a silicone-free routine after color services. Because there is no dimethicone or similar occlusive silicone in the mix, the finish leans toward softness and manageability rather than the slick, glassy feel that silicone-forward masks can produce, and very coarse or severely damaged hair may want to follow it with a leave-in or oil for extra slip.

Directions call for massaging the mask through hair after shampooing and leaving it on for five to ten minutes before rinsing, used weekly or every other week in place of a regular conditioner. That shorter contact time is convenient for a regular wash-day routine, though it also means the mask functions as a maintenance step rather than an intensive overnight repair treatment for severely over-processed hair.

Because the line is built around protein and moisture balance, the brand's own routine guidance often pairs this mask with a matching shampoo, conditioner, and treatment oil rather than positioning it as a single stand-alone fix, so shoppers comparing one jar against a full system should factor that into value expectations.
pros: Formulated with Briogeo's NOVA Complex (B-vitamins, rosehip and argan oils, algae, biotin) aimed at dry, damaged hair
Free of sulfates, silicones, and phthalates, and described as 98% naturally derived
Stated by the brand to be safe for color-treated, keratin-treated, and relaxed hair
cons: The five-to-ten-minute contact time may feel less intensive than longer-sit treatments for severely damaged hair
Brand guidance frames it as part of a broader Don't Despair, Repair! system rather than a stand-alone fix for extreme damage
products.bestFor: Color-treated hair that needs a sulfate- and silicone-free weekly conditioning mask focused on moisture-protein balance.

comparisons.title: Olaplex Nº.8 Bond Intense Moisture Mask vs. Briogeo Don't Despair, Repair! Deep Conditioning Mask
comparisons.subtitle: Comparing two weekly hair masks for dry, color-treated hair
comparisons.winnerReason: Briogeo's sulfate-, silicone-, and phthalate-free formula is explicitly stated by the brand to be safe for color-treated hair and avoids the dimethicone found in Olaplex's mask, making it a gentler weekly fit for dye-processed strands, though Olaplex remains a reasonable choice for anyone who wants a smaller dose of bond-building technology in the same step.
comparisons.verdict: Both masks function as a weekly, in-shower conditioning step rather than a leave-in treatment. Choose Briogeo's Don't Despair, Repair! mask if you want a sulfate-, silicone-, and phthalate-free formula the brand positions specifically for color-treated and chemically treated hair. Choose Olaplex Nº.8 if you already use a separate bond-building treatment like Nº.3 and want a moisturizing mask that still carries a smaller dose of the same technology alongside ceramides and hyaluronic acid.
